Subject: FinHealth / Redwood — Private VPC discovery recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — really appreciated the walkthrough. Below is a short recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points:
- Regulated data: PHI in prompts/outputs; must remain in FinHealth-controlled network and logging regime.
- Strict key management: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) required, no plaintext key export.
- Network constraints: limited outbound egress; strict firewall rules; potential air-gapped environments for some internal teams.
- Audit & retention: 7-year retention policy for audit logs and ability to produce audit trails.

Current stack / constraints:
- Core infra: AWS us-east-1 with VPCs isolated per product; EKS for orchestration.
- Identity: Okta SSO, use of AWS KMS (planned migration to HSM for some workloads).
- Security: in-house DLP layer and IDS monitoring. No third-party hosted data leaves VPC without explicit controls.

Success criteria for initial POC:
1) Private deployment (VPC) that keeps inference inside FinHealth network or via a dedicated private peering link.
2) Integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM for model keys and any secret material.
3) Proof of low-risk network posture: documented firewall rules / allowed endpoints and cert-backed mutual TLS.
4) Demonstrate latency & throughput targets for sample workload (~100 concurrent sessions, 2k token per session peaks).
5) Provide SOC2 artefacts and gap plan for any open items.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa / Redwood: share Private/VPC checklist + sample network diagram (attached). (By Wed 6/17)
- FinHealth: share security contact and network egress rules / whitelist. (By Fri 6/19)
- Schedule technical deep-dive with SE + infra (1-2 hrs) to validate peering and KMS integration. Target week of 6/22.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx, FinHealth_Security_Questions.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with meeting invites once we pick a slot.
